source.text: צַדִּ֣יק יְ֭הוָה בְּ/כָל דְּרָכָ֑י/ו וְ֝/חָסִ֗יד בְּ/כָל מַעֲשָֽׂי/ו־־׃

translation.text: Yahweh is righteous in all his ways and loyal in all his deeds[a].

footnotes.text: Or 'kind,' 'gracious,' or 'faithful.' Hebrew חסיד expresses loyalty or kindness. Greek ὅσιος, often rendered 'holy,' can interpret this same Hebrew adjective; it does not establish a different Hebrew reading.

lexical_decisions.rationale: The source contains the Tetragrammaton YHWH. Per project doctrine, it is rendered 'Yahweh,' preserving the personal divine name rather than substituting the title 'the LORD.'
The adjective denotes moral rightness/uprightness. 'Righteous' best preserves the covenantal and theological sense in praise language; 'just' is possible but narrower and less natural here.
Here ב marks sphere/reference: the LORD is righteous in the entirety of his ways. 'In all' is idiomatic and sufficiently formal.
'Ways' is the standard and contextually fitting rendering for דרכים in reference to God's manner of acting. It preserves the metaphor without over-interpreting.

Loyal expresses the adjective's loyalty/kindness range. This verse and the 11Q5 nun line use the same second colon; identical English wording makes that repetition visible. Greek hosios is an interpretive rendering, not proof of a different Hebrew adjective. No new HALOT consultation is claimed.
Deeds naturally denotes God's actions here and preserves the repeated expression in the provisionally included nun line. This is an English consistency choice, not changed Hebrew.

theological_decisions.issue: Rendering of חָסִיד in reference to God's character
theological_decisions.rationale: Retain the Masoretic חסיד and render loyalty/kindness explicitly. The identical second colon is rendered identically in the selected nun line. English holy and Greek hosios do not independently demonstrate a different underlying Hebrew word; the former categorical textual-tradition claim is removed.
theological_decisions.doctrine_reference: Preserve theological tension rather than resolve it; Original-language primacy over translation tradition.

legacy_source_audit.scope: WLC Hebrew, immediate literary context, natural-English and interpretation-boundary review
legacy_source_audit.review_summary: חָסִיד describes one characterized by חֶסֶד. Bare “faithful” can suggest only reliability and does not adequately represent the term’s loyal-kindness dimension. “Faithful in love” is natural in this praise context and preserves both constancy and benevolence without importing “holy,” which is not the WLC reading.

revisions.from: Yahweh is righteous in all his ways and faithful in all his works[a].
revisions.to: Yahweh is righteous in all his ways and loyal in all his deeds[a].
revisions.rationale: Keep source unchanged, make the repeated Hebrew colon explicit through identical English wording, and remove the unsupported inference from Greek hosios or English holy to different Hebrew consonants.
